summary:
Labuan is a federal territory of Malaysia and stands under the national framework: the federal Penal Code, the federal rules governing identity documents and federal immigration rules apply here as they do elsewhere in the country. One source, the Human Dignity Trust Malaysia country profile last updated 16 December 2025, states directly that the federal framework governs what a visitor faces in Labuan.

No arrest, raid, prosecution or act of violence against a transgender person in Labuan is documented in this inventory, and no local enforcement practice, local religious-police unit or local prosecution is recorded. The national assessment therefore applies to Labuan.
tangentialFactors:
The enforcement incidents the inventory does document all occurred outside Labuan: an October 2022 raid on a Queer Halloween party in Kuala Lumpur with at least 20 LGBT people arrested, an August 2022 raid on an LGBT venue with twenty men arrested, a Terengganu Sharia court ordering a lesbian couple caned, and November 2023 plans in Johor for conversion-therapy centres. Labuan appears in none of them.

The federal-territory Sharia-code finding in the Human Rights Watch and Justice for Sisters material is stated for Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya and is not extended to Labuan, so it cannot be read across to this territory.
localsOnly: No Labuan-specific resident-facing fact is recorded: the inventory names no local enactment, no local enforcement body and no case involving a transgender resident of the territory. Residents of Labuan live under the same national framework described for Malaysia as a whole, and the sources draw no distinction for them.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Labuan has its own Sharia enactment addressing same-sex conduct or gender nonconformity, and which body would enforce it, is not sourced in this inventory. The only federal-territory Sharia finding available is stated for Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.

The inventory carries no Labuan-specific enforcement data, incident reporting or survey coverage. The figures it does hold, 73 LGBT people interviewed across Malaysia from 2018 to 2021 and 1,733 attendees at government-run rehabilitation programmes as of June 2021, are national in scope and are not broken down for Labuan, so they say nothing about conditions in this territory.

Whether transgender visitors to Labuan face document-marker checks or gender-related screening at entry is not addressed by any source in this inventory; the only entry-related statement available for the country is a 2001 remark about gay foreign officials, which is carried at the national level.
